title: Buffered vs Unbuffered Channels in Go

scenes.say: Ever wonder when to use buffered versus unbuffered channels in Go? Let’s break it down.

scenes.label: Blocks
scenes.sub: Sender waits until receiver is ready.
scenes.say: With unbuffered channels, the sender blocks until a receiver is ready. This means both goroutines must sync up.

scenes.label: Async
scenes.sub: Send up to buffer size without blocking.
scenes.say: Buffered channels let you send messages up to their buffer size without blocking. This allows asynchronous communication.

scenes.code:
ch := make(chan int, 2)
ch <- 1
ch <- 2 // No block yet
scenes.say: For example, here we create a buffered channel with size two. Both sends succeed immediately, no waiting.

scenes.question: Buffered channels never block, right?
scenes.right: No, they block once the buffer is full.
scenes.say: Interview trap: Buffered channels do block, but only when the buffer is full. Don’t forget that.
